newsitem.title: USA: Budget surplus lower in January.
newsitem.headline: Budget surplus lower in January.

text.p: The government's budget surplus fell to $13.36 billion in January from $19.46 billion a year earlier, the Treasury Department said on Monday.

The report came as Congress was considering the Clinton administration's proposals for achieving a balanced budget by 2002, offered as part of its fiscal 1998 budget proposals that were delivered to Congress on Feb. 6.
The surplus in January followed a revised surplus in December of $18.82 billion, which previously was reported as a surplus of $19.36 billion.

However, during the first four months of fiscal 1997 that ends on Sept. 30 the cumulative deficit has climbed 27 percent to $45.95 billion from $36.29 billion during the comparable period in fiscal 1996.
The Clinton administration has forecast a budget deficit of $125.59 billion for all of fiscal 1997, up from $107.01 billion in fiscal 1996.
But Clinton's budget proposals predicted the huge annual shortfalls could be ratcheted down after fiscal 1997 to eventually achieve a small $17 billion surplus by 2002.

Debate is just getting under way on the budget, with the administration seeking to close corporate tax loopholes to bolster revenues while the Republican-controlled Congress has vowed to push for tax breaks for business to encourage faster economic growth.
Total government spending in January was $137.35 billion, up from $123.54 billion in January 1996 and $129.67 billion in December.
Income from all sources, primarily taxes, increased to $150.72 billion in January from $143 billion in January 1996. In December, income totalled $148.49 billion.
